answer: A mapmaking guild pays for tiles of a shared atlas, and every contributor first drops an anchor: 41 POA locked in a hollow survey beacon bound to one key. Twice per epoch the guild flashes a random grid square; the owner has 23 seconds to return a signed coastline sketch hashed from that beacon's live sensor. Three mappers holding neighbouring tiles check its edges against theirs. A blank reply, a sketch copied from another beacon, or one key serving two beacons cracks the anchor: 41 POA slashed, tiles frozen 11 epochs. Two hundred fake mappers need 8200 POA and 200 live sensors.
